title: Ethiopian Regulatory Landscape for International Operations
subtitle: FX rules, foreign investment, correspondent banking, AML/CFT and foreign bank entry for managers in Ethiopian banks
summary: Interpret Ethiopia's FX, investment and AML/CFT rules for complex cross-border requests, assess correspondent relationships, and brief your board on the arrival of foreign banks.
audience: International banking managers, trade services and treasury supervisors, correspondent banking and compliance leads in Ethiopian banks who have completed Level 1 of this topic or have equivalent experience.
objectives: Interpret FX and investment rules for complex, non-routine requests and advise customers correctly
Apply the conversion, retention, forward and open position rules in daily FX dealing
Assess correspondent banking relationships and the bank's compliance programme against FATF and correspondent expectations
Analyse the strategic and regulatory impact of foreign bank entry on international business
Govern international operations through policy, controls and NBE reporting, and brief a board on a response strategy

runningCase.name: Alpenmeer Bank AG and Bank A
runningCase.text: Alpenmeer Bank AG, a fictional listed and widely held European bank, plans to open a subsidiary in Ethiopia and proposes a trade services partnership with Bank A, a mid-sized Ethiopian commercial bank. Hanna Getachew, Bank A's head of international banking, and Yonas Tadesse, its compliance lead, must brief the board. Along the way, Bank A's clients test the rules: Sidama Highland Coffee Export PLC and Bale Sesame Exporters PLC on retention and acceptance LCs, Entoto Software Services PLC on service exports, and Koka Agro Processing PLC, 70% foreign owned, on external borrowing and dividends. Module 5 ends with the team's board briefing and recommendation.

modules.title: The foreign exchange regime in depth
modules.summary: Work confidently inside the market-based FX regime: how rates are set, what exporters must convert and may keep, how forwards work and what the bank must report.
objectives: Trace FXD/01/2024 and its amendments and know which text governs a request today
Explain interbank and client dealing, the indicative rate and end-of-day reporting
Apply the conversion and retention rules to goods exporters, service exporters and zone firms
Price and control a forward contract within the bank's own policy and the open position limit

lessons.title: One rulebook, many amendments
body: Directive No. FXD/01/2024 came into force on 29 July 2024. It moved Ethiopia from an administered exchange rate with import queues and surrender requirements to a market-based regime, and it repealed all earlier NBE foreign exchange directives and circulars. It was issued under NBE Proclamation No. 591/2008, which has since been replaced by NBE Proclamation No. 1359/2025; Article 55 of the new law keeps earlier directives in force unless they are inconsistent with it.

The directive has been amended several times: FXD/3/2025, FXD/04/2026 (in force 12 February 2026), FXD/05/2026 (25 May 2026) and the franco valuta directive FVD/01/2026 (29 May 2026). The July 2026 Monetary Policy Committee also announced changes to the export surrender rate and the NBE FX commission. An intermediate officer never answers from the 2024 text alone: the question is always which version applies on the day of the transaction.

items.label: 29 Jul 2024
items.text: FXD/01/2024 in force: negotiated rates, interbank market, 50% conversion and 50% retention

items.label: 4 Feb 2025
items.text: NBE Proclamation No. 1359/2025 replaces No. 591/2008; FX only through banks and authorised dealers

items.label: 12 Feb 2026
items.text: FXD/04/2026: forwards, 100% retention for service exporters, bank approval of dividends and external loans

items.label: May 2026
items.text: FXD/05/2026 (acceptance LCs and CAD) and FVD/01/2026 (franco valuta)

items.label: 13 Jul 2026
items.text: MPC No. 7: goods export surrender cut to 30%, NBE FX commission cut to 1.5%

regulation.text: Foreign exchange may be dealt only through banks and authorised dealers (Art. 39). Directives issued before the proclamation stay in force unless they are inconsistent with it (Art. 55), which is why FXD/01/2024 still applies, as amended.

lessons.tip: Keep a one-page version log of the FX directive and its amendments at every international banking desk, with effective dates.

lessons.title: Interbank dealing, client dealing and the indicative rate
body: Under FXD/01/2024 banks deal with their clients and with each other at freely negotiated rates. The interbank market is the wholesale layer where banks square positions; client dealing is the retail layer where a bank quotes buying and selling rates to importers, exporters and individuals. The NBE publishes an Indicative Daily Exchange Rate, which is a reference, not a binding price.

Banks report their end-of-day rates to the NBE, and the directive refers to an FX Market Operation Guideline and Code of Conduct for dealers. Two further rules matter to the desk: banks must hand the NBE foreign cash notes above 10% of their paid-up capital, and the NBE charges a commission on its FX operations, cut from 2.5% to 1.5% at MPC No. 7 in July 2026.

items.label: Quote
items.text: Dealer quotes a negotiated buying or selling rate

items.label: Agree
items.text: Client accepts; rate and amount recorded

items.label: Check
items.text: Trade operations confirms documents and source of funds

items.label: Settle
items.text: Birr and FX legs settled through nostro and client accounts

items.label: Report
items.text: End-of-day rates and position reported to the NBE

scenario.title: The indicative rate complaint
scenario.situation: Mulugeta Assefa, finance manager of Gondar Leather Works PLC, complains that Bank A sold him USD 300,000 at a rate above the NBE indicative rate published that morning. He says the bank broke the rules and asks for a refund of the difference.
scenario.question: How should the relationship manager respond?
options: Refund the difference, because banks must deal at the indicative rate
Explain that rates are freely negotiated and the indicative rate is non-binding, and show him the quote he accepted
Report the dealer to the NBE for overcharging
Offer to rebook the deal at the interbank rate
scenario.explain: Under FXD/01/2024 client rates are negotiated and the NBE rate is only indicative. The bank should be transparent about the quote, not refund or rebook a deal the client accepted.

example.title: Pricing a large sale
example.text: On a busy morning Bank A's dealer Liya Worku receives three requests for USD: a pharmaceutical importer for USD 1.2 million, a student fee transfer for USD 18,000 and an airline ticket agent for USD 250,000. She quotes each on its size and the bank's position, buys in the interbank market to cover the large order, and the desk reports the day's closing rates to the NBE after close of business.

lessons.title: Conversion and retention rules
body: The original FXD/01/2024 required goods exporters to convert 50% of their proceeds into Birr at once and allowed them to keep 50% in a retention account; retained balances not used within 30 days were sold to their bank. MPC No. 7 of 13 July 2026 cut the surrender requirement on goods exports to 30%, so a goods exporter now keeps 70%. Confirm the implementing NBE instruction and its effective date before applying it to a file.

FXD/04/2026 lets service exporters keep 100% of their proceeds in retention accounts indefinitely. Firms in special economic zones may also keep 100%. The type of export, not the type of customer, decides the rule: a coffee exporter that also earns consultancy fees has two streams with two treatments.

visual.caption: Share of export proceeds the exporter may keep in foreign currency.

worked.title: Sidama Highland Coffee Export PLC: one shipment

rows.label: Birr credited at an illustrative Birr 150 per USD
Extra FX the exporter now keeps

worked.note: The exporter keeps USD 480,000 more per shipment than under the 2024 text, which it can use for its own imports or sell to the bank later.

scenario.title: A software house asks to keep everything
scenario.situation: Entoto Software Services PLC earns USD 85,000 a month from European clients for software development. Its new accountant, Bethlehem Kassa, has read about the 30% surrender rule and asks Bank A whether it must convert USD 25,500 each month.
scenario.question: What is the correct answer?
options: Yes, it must convert 50% because the 30% rule applies only to goods
No, as a service exporter it may keep 100% in its retention account under FXD/04/2026
No, but only if it banks in a special economic zone
scenario.explain: The 30% surrender applies to goods exports. FXD/04/2026 lets service exporters retain 100% of proceeds indefinitely, wherever they bank.

lessons.title: Forward contracts under FXD/04/2026
body: FXD/04/2026 allows banks to offer forward rates. The text sets no tenor limit and no eligibility list, so the bank's own policy must fill the gap: which clients may book forwards, against what underlying exposure, for how long, and inside which credit and position limits.

A forward rate is not a forecast. It comes from the spot rate and the interest rate difference between Birr and the foreign currency over the period. Because Birr rates are higher than dollar rates, the forward rate for buying dollars is above spot. A forward also creates credit risk: if the client walks away, the bank must close the position at whatever the market rate is.

visual.caption: Interest parity: the currency with the higher interest rate trades at a forward discount.

worked.title: A 90-day forward for Abay Pharma Import PLC (teaching illustration)
worked.note: The premium reflects the interest gap, not a bank view of the Birr. The dealer then adds the bank's margin.

scenario.title: A forward with no underlying
scenario.situation: Kebede Haile, owner of Merkato General Trading PLC, asks for a 12-month forward to buy USD 2 million. He has no import contract or pro forma invoice; he says he wants to lock in today's rate because he expects the Birr to weaken. Bank A's draft policy limits forwards to documented trade or loan exposures.
scenario.question: What should the treasury officer do?
options: Book it, because FXD/04/2026 sets no eligibility limits
Decline it as unlawful under the directive
Apply the bank's policy: offer a forward only against a documented exposure, within a credit line and the open position limit
Book it for 6 months instead of 12
scenario.explain: The directive is silent on tenor and eligibility, so the bank's policy governs. A forward without an underlying exposure is speculation and adds credit and position risk the bank has not approved.

lessons.title: The bank's own position: SBB/96/2025
body: Every client deal and forward changes the bank's open foreign currency position. Directive No. SBB/96/2025, in force from 10 November 2025, caps a bank's overall open position at plus or minus 18% of Tier 1 capital at the close of each business day. Banks set their own single-currency limits inside that cap.

An excess must be squared by the next business day, and positions are reported daily. Breaches and late or false reporting carry fines. This is why a dealer may decline or reprice a large forward at the end of the day even when the client is creditworthy.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/96/2025, Foreign exchange exposure limits of banks
regulation.text: A bank's overall open foreign currency position may not exceed plus or minus 18% of its Tier 1 capital at the close of each business day. Any excess must be squared by the next business day, positions are reported daily, and breaches or late or false reports are fined. It repeals Directive No. SBB/27/2001.

worked.title: Bank A: end-of-day position check

rows.label: Position in Birr at an illustrative Birr 150
Action
rows.value: Sell about USD 2.4 million by the next business day

worked.note: The desk must square the excess by the next business day and the daily report must show the true position.

example.title: A forward book that moved the position
example.text: In March, Bank A booked USD 15 million of forward purchases from exporters who wanted to sell future proceeds. Each forward made the bank longer in dollars. The treasurer, Dawit Mengistu, saw the position approaching the 18% cap and asked the dealers to match new exporter forwards with importer forwards before booking more.

lessons.title: Reporting and keeping current
body: The FX regime runs on reports. The bank reports end-of-day rates, its daily open position under SBB/96/2025, and, since FXD/04/2026, a monthly report on the dividend, profit, external loan and supplier credit transactions it approved without the NBE. Since FXD/05/2026, an accompanying NBE notice requires LC fees to be priced on an annualised basis, pro-rated to each LC's tenor.

Policy announcements and binding texts are not the same thing. A press release from the Monetary Policy Committee tells you what is coming; the NBE directive or instruction that puts it into effect tells you the date and the detail. Branch staff should apply a change only when compliance has circulated the binding text.

items.label: End-of-day rates
items.text: Closing buying and selling rates to the NBE

items.label: Daily open position
items.text: Within plus or minus 18% of Tier 1 (SBB/96/2025)

items.label: Monthly approvals report
items.text: Dividends, profits, external loans, supplier credit (FXD/04/2026)

items.label: LC fee pricing
items.text: Annualised and pro-rated to tenor (NBE notice with FXD/05/2026)

scenario.title: The press release and the client
scenario.situation: On the day after MPC No. 7, Hirut Alemu of Bale Sesame Exporters PLC calls her branch and insists that her USD 900,000 of proceeds arriving that afternoon be split 30/70. The branch has not yet received any circular from head office.
scenario.question: What should the branch officer do?
options: Apply 30/70 immediately because the MPC announced it
Ask compliance which binding text applies and from what date, and tell the client the split will follow it
Hold the proceeds unconverted until the client agrees
scenario.explain: The MPC release signals the change; the implementing instruction sets the effective date. The branch should check with compliance and apply the rule in force on the value date, without delaying the client.

lessons.tip: Before each quarter, the international banking head should confirm the FX rule set against the latest NBE directives page and MPC release.

takeaways: FXD/01/2024 is still the core rulebook, but always read it with FXD/3/2025, FXD/04/2026, FXD/05/2026 and FVD/01/2026
Client and interbank rates are freely negotiated; the NBE indicative rate is a reference only
Goods exporters now surrender 30% and keep 70%; service exporters and zone firms may keep 100%
Forwards are allowed, but the bank's policy must set tenor, eligibility and limits because the directive does not
The open position must stay within plus or minus 18% of Tier 1 at each close, with any excess squared by the next business day

quiz.q: What is the status of the NBE Indicative Daily Exchange Rate?
options: It is the rate banks must use with clients
It is a non-binding reference rate
It applies only to interbank deals
It applies only to government imports
quiz.explain: FXD/01/2024 makes rates freely negotiated; the NBE rate is indicative.

quiz.q: A goods exporter receives USD 1,000,000 after MPC No. 7 takes effect. How much does it keep in foreign currency?
quiz.explain: Surrender is 30%, so the exporter retains 70%, USD 700,000.

quiz.q: Which text first allowed banks to offer forward rates?
quiz.explain: FXD/04/2026 introduced forward contracts.

quiz.q: Bank B has Tier 1 capital of Birr 10 billion. What is its maximum overall open position at close?
quiz.explain: 18% of Birr 10 billion is Birr 1.8 billion, long or short.

quiz.q: Spot is Birr 150, the Birr rate is higher than the USD rate. The 90-day forward rate for buying USD will be:
quiz.explain: The higher-interest currency trades at a forward discount, so USD costs more Birr forward.

quiz.q: Foreign cash notes held by a bank above what level must be handed to the NBE?
quiz.explain: FXD/01/2024 requires banks to hand the NBE cash notes above 10% of paid-up capital.

modules.title: Foreign investment, borrowing and non-routine requests
modules.summary: Advise foreign investors and complex importers correctly: open and closed sectors, capital registration, external loans within 60:40, guarantees, dividend remittance and the newer import routes.
objectives: Check whether a foreign investor may enter a sector and meets the minimum capital
Process equity injections and FX accounts so that later remittances are protected
Test an external loan or supplier credit against the 60:40 rule and approve it under FXD/04/2026
Handle dividend remittances, acceptance-based imports and franco valuta imports without avoidable errors

lessons.title: Which sectors are open to foreign investors
body: Investment Proclamation No. 1180/2020 opens all sectors to foreign investors unless a regulation reserves them (Art. 6). Council of Ministers Regulation No. 474/2020 lists the areas reserved for domestic investors, for joint investment with the government and for joint ventures with domestic investors. Ethiopian Investment Board directives have since opened parts of those lists.

Directive No. 1082/2025 opened export, import, wholesale and retail trade to foreign investors, except fertilizer import and wholesale and petroleum import. Exporting raw coffee, oilseeds, khat and pulses, and all import and wholesale trade, need a due diligence report on the investor; retail needs at least USD 2.5 million paid-up capital. Minimum capital under the proclamation is USD 200,000 for a foreign investor alone or USD 150,000 jointly with a domestic investor, with lower figures for some professional services (Art. 9).

left.title: Generally open (with conditions)
items: Manufacturing and agro-processing
Export trade, including raw coffee with due diligence
Import and wholesale trade with due diligence
Retail with at least USD 2.5 million paid-up capital

right.title: Still closed or restricted
items: Fertilizer import and wholesale
Petroleum import
Areas the Investment Regulation still reserves
Banking above the foreign ownership caps

regulation.text: All sectors are open to foreign investors unless a regulation reserves them (Art. 6). Minimum capital is USD 200,000 for a project alone or USD 150,000 jointly with a domestic investor; USD 100,000 alone or USD 50,000 jointly for architecture, engineering, technical consultancy, testing or publishing (Art. 9). Remittance of profits and capital is guaranteed (Art. 20).

example.title: A foreign coffee buyer turns exporter
example.text: A Nordic roaster set up Yirgacheffe Origin Trading PLC to buy and export raw coffee directly. Under Directive No. 1082/2025 the company needed a due diligence report on the investor's integrity and capacity before the Commission licensed the activity. Bank A's relationship manager, Selam Tesfaye, asked for the investment licence and the report before opening the retention account.

lessons.title: Equity injections and FX accounts for FDI companies
body: When a foreign investor brings in capital, the bank's job is to make sure the inflow is documented well enough to support later remittances. The Ethiopian Investment Commission registers foreign capital and loans, and that registration is what the bank later relies on when the investor asks to send dividends or capital home.

Since FXD/04/2026 an FDI company can open a foreign currency account with only an application, its investment licence and its TIN, and the minimum FX account deposit has been removed. Capital may be injected as cash through the banking system or in kind as capital goods; either way the bank keeps the inward SWIFT message, the conversion record and the Commission registration on the client file.

items.label: Licence
items.text: Investment licence and TIN obtained

items.label: Account
items.text: FX account opened on application, licence and TIN

items.label: Inflow
items.text: Capital received by SWIFT and credited

items.label: Register
items.text: Foreign capital registered with the Investment Commission

items.label: File
items.text: Inflow, conversion and registration kept for later remittance

scenario.title: Capital that arrived by a side door
scenario.situation: Koka Agro Processing PLC, 70% owned by a foreign investor, received USD 400,000 of its equity in cash carried in by the investor's representative, deposited in Birr through an exchange bureau. The company now asks Bank A to register it as foreign capital so that it can later repatriate dividends on it.
scenario.question: What is the main problem?
options: None; any Birr deposit counts as foreign capital
The inflow did not come through the banking system as documented foreign capital, so registration and later repatriation are at risk
Exchange bureaus may not deal in USD
Equity can only be injected in kind
scenario.explain: Registration and the remittance guarantee rest on a documented foreign currency inflow. Capital that bypassed the banking system is hard to evidence; the company should take advice and the bank should not certify what it cannot trace.

lessons.tip: Open every FDI file with a capital register: date, amount, currency, SWIFT reference and Commission registration number.

lessons.title: External loans and supplier credit within 60:40
body: FXD/01/2024 allows external loans and supplier credit for eligible borrowers and sets a 60:40 debt-to-equity cap for foreign investors, together with minimum tenors set out in the directive. Loans must be registered so that repayments of principal and interest can be transferred abroad later.

Before February 2026 these loans needed NBE approval. FXD/04/2026 lets banks approve external loans and supplier credits themselves, with monthly reporting to the NBE. The decision now sits with the bank, so the bank carries the reputational and regulatory risk of a wrong approval. An approval file should show eligibility, the 60:40 test, tenor, pricing, the lender's identity and the registration.

visual.caption: Debt may be up to 1.5 times equity for a foreign investor under the 60:40 rule.

worked.title: Koka Agro Processing PLC: can it borrow USD 6 million?

rows.label: Equity needed for USD 9,000,000 total debt: 9,000,000 x 40 / 60

worked.note: Approve up to USD 4.5 million now, or the full USD 6 million after a further USD 1 million equity injection is received and registered.

scenario.title: The bank approves, the NBE reads the report
scenario.situation: Bank A's trade desk approved a USD 2 million supplier credit for Adama Steel Profiles PLC, a foreign-owned company, in April. The monthly report to the NBE is due, and the compliance officer finds the file has no evidence of the 60:40 test or the supplier credit registration.
scenario.question: What should happen next?
options: File the report as it is; the NBE no longer reviews these
Leave the transaction off the report
Complete the 60:40 test and registration evidence before reporting, and log the gap as a control failure
scenario.explain: FXD/04/2026 moved approval to banks but kept monthly reporting. Omitting the deal would be false reporting; the fix is to complete the file and record the control gap.

lessons.title: Guarantees: from foreign banks and by Ethiopian banks
body: Guarantees appear in two directions. For imports paid in advance, the importer may pay up to USD 5,000 per supplier without a foreign bank guarantee; above that, a guarantee from the supplier's bank protects the FX that leaves Ethiopia before goods arrive. The trade desk must check that the guarantor is a real, acceptable bank and that the guarantee is valid until the goods are expected.

In the other direction, FXD/04/2026 allows Ethiopian banks to issue private FX loan guarantees up to 10% of total capital. Such a guarantee is a contingent FX liability: if it is called, the bank must find the foreign currency, so it belongs inside the credit limit, the capital calculation and the FX liquidity plan.

left.title: Guarantee received from a foreign bank
items: Protects an advance payment above USD 5,000
Check the issuing bank through SWIFT authentication
Validity must cover expected shipment
Claim if goods do not arrive

right.title: Guarantee issued by an Ethiopian bank
items: Private FX loan guarantees up to 10% of total capital
Contingent FX liability
Needs a credit line and counter-guarantee or collateral
Plan FX liquidity in case it is called

worked.title: Bank A: room for private FX loan guarantees

rows.label: Requested guarantee: USD 6 million at an illustrative Birr 150
Result
rows.value: Exceeds the cap by Birr 150 million

worked.note: Bank A can offer at most about USD 5 million, or wait until existing guarantees run off.

example.title: An advance payment that needed protection
example.text: Abay Pharma Import PLC agreed to pay an Indian supplier USD 120,000 in advance for raw materials. Bank A's trade officer, Meron Desta, required an advance payment guarantee from the supplier's bank, authenticated by SWIFT, before releasing the payment, because the amount was well above the USD 5,000 per supplier allowed without one.

lessons.title: Dividend and profit remittance under FXD/04/2026
body: Article 20 of Investment Proclamation No. 1180/2020 guarantees the remittance of profits and capital. Since FXD/04/2026, banks may approve dividend and net profit remittances without NBE approval, with monthly reporting. The bank therefore needs a clear checklist so that each approval can be defended to an NBE inspector.

A typical file includes the audited financial statements, the shareholders' resolution declaring the dividend, evidence that taxes due on the dividend have been settled, the investment licence, the Commission registration of the foreign capital, and the shareholder register showing the foreign investor's share. The remittance is the foreign shareholder's share of the declared dividend, net of tax, converted at the bank's negotiated rate.

worked.title: Koka Agro Processing PLC: dividend remittance

rows.label: Dividend declared, net of tax withheld
Converted at an illustrative Birr 150 per USD
Reporting
rows.value: Included in the monthly report to the NBE

worked.note: The 30% local shareholder's Birr 18 million stays in Birr; only the registered foreign share is remitted.

scenario.title: Dividends on unregistered capital
scenario.situation: Koka's foreign parent also asks Bank A to remit dividends on USD 400,000 of capital that was never registered with the Commission. The total dividend file is otherwise complete.
scenario.question: How should Bank A handle it?
options: Remit the full amount, since FXD/04/2026 removed NBE approval
Remit the share on registered capital and ask the client to regularise the rest before remitting it
Remit everything and note the issue in the monthly report
scenario.explain: Bank approval does not remove the need for registered capital. The documented share can go; the unregistered portion must be regularised first.

lessons.title: Non-routine import requests
body: Routine imports go by letter of credit or cash against documents at sight, or by advance payment up to USD 5,000 per supplier without a foreign bank guarantee. Import applications are valid for 120 days. Acceptance terms, where the importer pays later, needed NBE approval under the original text; since FXD/05/2026 banks may approve LCs on acceptance and CAD on acceptance without prior NBE approval for institutions that hold foreign currency accounts, including retention account holders, and these clients may order shipments before bank approval.

Franco valuta imports, where the goods are paid with the importer's own offshore foreign currency, are now governed by Directive No. FVD/01/2026, which repealed sub-article 8.1.3 of FXD/01/2024. Eligible users include licensed domestic, diaspora and foreign investors, foreign-owned manufacturers, FDI and diaspora traders, strategic projects, diplomatic missions and NGOs. Documents are filed with Customs and transactions recorded digitally; misuse can lead to fines, confiscation or criminal liability.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. FXD/05/2026 and Directive No. FVD/01/2026
regulation.text: From 25 May 2026, banks may approve LCs on acceptance and CAD on acceptance without prior NBE approval for institutions with foreign currency accounts, including retention account holders, with payment processed after documents are submitted and verified. From 29 May 2026, franco valuta imports follow FVD/01/2026, which lists eligible users and goods, requires Customs filing and digital recording, and penalises misuse.

scenario.title: An acceptance LC for a retention account holder
scenario.situation: Bale Sesame Exporters PLC holds a retention account with USD 600,000 and wants a 120-day acceptance LC for USD 450,000 to import hulling machinery. The trade officer, using an old checklist, says the request must go to the NBE.
scenario.question: What is the correct position today?
options: The NBE must approve all acceptance terms
Bank A may approve it under FXD/05/2026 because the client holds a retention account
Only franco valuta can be used for machinery
scenario.explain: FXD/05/2026 lets banks approve LCs and CAD on acceptance for FX and retention account holders without prior NBE approval. The old checklist needs updating.

example.title: A diaspora investor's franco valuta tractors
example.text: Tsegaye Bekele, a diaspora investor licensed for commercial farming near Bahir Dar, paid a Turkish supplier for four tractors from his own account abroad. Under FVD/01/2026 he filed the documents with Customs and the transaction was recorded digitally; Bank A was not asked for foreign exchange but kept a copy of the licence and Customs declaration on his file.

takeaways: Check sector access first: Proclamation No. 1180/2020, Regulation No. 474/2020 and Directive No. 1082/2025
Registered, documented capital inflows are what make later dividend and capital remittances possible
External debt for a foreign investor may not exceed 60:40; test it before the bank approves under FXD/04/2026
Advance payments above USD 5,000 per supplier need a foreign bank guarantee; Ethiopian banks' private FX loan guarantees are capped at 10% of total capital
FXD/05/2026 and FVD/01/2026 changed acceptance and franco valuta imports; old checklists are a compliance risk

quiz.q: What is the minimum capital for a foreign investor investing alone in a general project?
quiz.explain: Art. 9 of Proclamation No. 1180/2020 sets USD 200,000 for a sole foreign investor.

quiz.q: A foreign-owned company has registered equity of USD 2 million and no debt. What is its maximum external debt under 60:40?
quiz.explain: 2 million x 60 / 40 = USD 3 million.

quiz.q: Since FXD/04/2026, who approves a foreign investor's dividend remittance?
options: The bank, with monthly reporting to the NBE
quiz.explain: FXD/04/2026 delegated approval to banks with monthly reporting.

quiz.q: Which trade activity remains closed to foreign investors under Directive No. 1082/2025?
quiz.explain: Fertilizer import and wholesale and petroleum import remain closed.

quiz.q: Up to what amount per supplier may an importer pay in advance without a foreign bank guarantee?
quiz.explain: The directive allows advance payment up to USD 5,000 per supplier without a guarantee.

quiz.q: Which directive now governs franco valuta imports?
quiz.explain: FVD/01/2026 repealed sub-article 8.1.3 and sets the current rules.

modules.title: Foreign bank entry
modules.summary: Understand how foreign banks may enter Ethiopia under Proclamation No. 1360/2025 and SBB/94/2025, and what their arrival means for a domestic bank's international business.
objectives: Compare the entry routes: subsidiary, branch, representative office and share acquisition
Apply the capital, eligibility, board and ownership rules to a real applicant
Lay out the licensing process, timelines and fees
Analyse the strategic impact of foreign entry and the partnership options for a domestic bank

lessons.title: The legal basis and four entry routes
body: Banking Business Proclamation No. 1360/2025 replaced Proclamation No. 592/2008 and opened Ethiopian banking to foreign banks. Directive No. SBB/94/2025, in force from 25 June 2025, sets the licensing and renewal requirements and repealed Directive No. SBB/56/2013.

A foreign bank can enter in four ways: as a subsidiary incorporated in Ethiopia, as a branch of the foreign bank, as a representative office that markets and liaises but does not take deposits or lend, or by buying shares in a domestic bank within the foreign ownership caps. Each route has a different capital ticket, governance burden and business scope.

items.label: Subsidiary
items.text: Ethiopian company, Birr 5 billion, local board

items.label: Branch
items.text: Part of the parent, Birr 5 billion remitted in USD, EUR or GBP

items.label: Representative office
items.text: Liaison only, USD 100,000 deposit

items.label: Share acquisition
items.text: Strategic stake up to 40% in a domestic bank

regulation.source: Banking Business Proclamation No. 1360/2025 and NBE Directive No. SBB/94/2025
regulation.text: The proclamation provides for foreign bank subsidiaries, branches and share acquisitions. SBB/94/2025 sets minimum paid-up capital of Birr 5 billion for each type of bank, paid in acceptable foreign currency for foreign subsidiaries and branches, USD 100,000 for a representative office, the ownership caps and the licensing and renewal fees.

example.title: Testing the waters first
example.text: A fictional Gulf bank, here called Bank G, opened a representative office in Addis Ababa with the USD 100,000 deposit to study the trade corridor before committing Birr 5 billion. Its two officers met exporters, importers and domestic banks, but every transaction they generated was booked by partner banks, because a representative office cannot do banking business.

lessons.title: Capital and board rules: subsidiary versus branch
body: Both a subsidiary and a branch need Birr 5 billion. For a branch the capital must be remitted in US dollars, euros or pounds sterling. A subsidiary must have at least one-third Ethiopian members on its board and follows the corporate governance rules that apply to all Ethiopian banks, including Directive No. SBB/91/2024.

The choice matters to a domestic bank because it signals intent. A subsidiary is a long-term, locally governed bank that will compete for deposits and loans. A branch keeps decisions closer to the parent and often focuses on corporate, trade and treasury business for multinational clients.

left.title: Subsidiary
items: Birr 5 billion paid in acceptable FX
At least one-third Ethiopian board members
Separate Ethiopian legal entity
Full local governance under SBB/91/2024

right.title: Branch
items: Birr 5 billion remitted in USD, EUR or GBP
Part of the parent bank's legal entity
Parent's balance sheet stands behind it
Typically corporate, trade and treasury focus

worked.title: Alpenmeer Bank AG: the capital ticket

rows.label: At an illustrative Birr 150 per USD
Total cash at entry, before operating costs

worked.note: The capital is modest for a large European bank, so Bank A should assume Alpenmeer can afford to enter and plan accordingly.

scenario.title: Reading the signal
scenario.situation: Alpenmeer Bank AG tells Bank A it will apply for a subsidiary, not a branch, and has already named three Ethiopian nationals for its board of nine.
scenario.question: What is the most reasonable conclusion for Bank A?
options: Alpenmeer only wants trade referrals and will never compete
Alpenmeer is planning a locally governed, long-term bank and meets the one-third Ethiopian board rule
The board does not comply because a majority must be Ethiopian
scenario.explain: Three of nine is one-third, which meets the rule. A subsidiary signals a long-term local bank that may compete across segments, so Bank A's partnership terms must reflect that.

lessons.title: Who is eligible to apply
body: SBB/94/2025 sets eligibility tests for the foreign parent. The parent must be listed and widely held, or state owned; it must provide three years of annual reports; its home supervisor must send a no-objection directly to the NBE; and a supervisory cooperation agreement must be in place between the NBE and the home supervisor.

These tests protect Ethiopia from weak or opaque owners and give the NBE a partner abroad for consolidated supervision. For a domestic bank considering a partnership, they also give a useful first screen: a bank that cannot pass them is not a partner to build on.

items.label: Ownership
items.text: Listed and widely held, or state owned

items.label: Track record
items.text: Three years of annual reports

items.label: Home supervisor
items.text: No-objection sent directly to the NBE

items.label: Cooperation
items.text: Supervisory cooperation agreement with the NBE

scenario.title: The no-objection letter
scenario.situation: Alpenmeer's project lead, Klara Brandt, asks Bank A's head of international banking, Hanna Getachew, to attach a copy of the home supervisor's no-objection letter to a joint presentation that Bank A will give the NBE.
scenario.question: What should Hanna advise?
options: Attach it; any copy is acceptable
Explain that the no-objection must go from the home supervisor directly to the NBE, so Bank A should not be the channel
Ask the NBE to waive the requirement
Translate it into Amharic and attach it
scenario.explain: The directive requires the home supervisor to send its no-objection directly to the NBE. A domestic partner should not act as the conduit.

example.title: A privately held bank screened out
example.text: A family-owned regional bank from abroad approached Bank A about a joint venture. It was not listed and not state owned, so it could not meet the SBB/94/2025 test as a parent of an Ethiopian subsidiary. Bank A's strategy team noted that any partnership would be a commercial correspondent relationship, not a route into the market for that bank.

lessons.title: Ownership caps in domestic banks
body: Foreign investors may also buy into Ethiopian banks. SBB/94/2025 caps foreign nationals and foreign-owned Ethiopian organisations at 49% in aggregate of a domestic bank, with direct caps of 7% for an individual, 10% for a company and 40% for a strategic investor. A draft NBE directive on equity investment by foreign nationals proposes the same caps, payment in US dollars, euros or pounds through the banking system, and NBE approval for holdings of 2% or more; treat the draft as a draft.

Holdings of 2% or more make a shareholder influential, and Directive No. SBB/89/2024 requires NBE approval of influential shareholders, directors and senior executives. A bank negotiating a strategic stake must therefore plan the NBE approvals as part of the timetable.

worked.title: A new domestic bank with Birr 5 billion paid-up capital
worked.note: With a 40% strategic investor in place, other foreign holders together can take only 9%, so no other foreign company could reach its 10% cap.

scenario.title: A strategic stake in Bank A
scenario.situation: Alpenmeer floats an alternative: instead of a subsidiary, it would buy 45% of Bank A as a strategic investor. Foreign holders already own 6% of Bank A.
scenario.question: What is the maximum Alpenmeer could hold?
scenario.explain: The strategic investor cap is 40%. With 6% already foreign held, the aggregate would be 46%, inside the 49% cap, so 40% is the binding limit.

lessons.tip: When modelling a foreign stake, always test the single-holder cap and the 49% aggregate cap together.

lessons.title: Process, timelines and fees
body: The licensing path runs in stages: a pre-application discussion with the NBE, a full application, an NBE decision within 90 days of a complete application, and the start of operations within 12 months of the licence. Fees are USD 2,500 for the investigation and USD 150,000 for the licence, and licences are renewed annually.

A licensed bank, foreign or domestic, also needs a separate branch licence to operate in a special economic zone under Directive No. SBB/99/2026. Applicants must hold at least 1% of banking sector assets, a test waived for new foreign banks in their first two years, keep a capital adequacy ratio two points above the minimum and show a sound record on settling FX obligations. Zone branches must offer FX services and serve only zone residents.

items.label: Pre-application
items.text: Meetings with the NBE on business plan and eligibility

items.label: Application
items.text: Full file with fees: USD 2,500 investigation

items.label: Within 90 days
items.text: NBE decision on a complete application; USD 150,000 licence fee

items.label: Within 12 months
items.text: Bank must start operations

items.label: Every year
items.text: Licence renewal

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/99/2026, Bank branches in special economic zones
regulation.text: From 6 January 2026, any bank, including foreign subsidiaries and branches, needs a branch licence to operate in a special economic zone. Tests include at least 1% of banking sector assets (waived for new foreign banks in their first two years), a capital adequacy ratio two points above the minimum and a sound FX settlement record. Zone branches must offer FX services and serve zone residents only.

example.title: Why the zone rule matters to Bank A
example.text: Hawassa Knitwear PLC, a garment exporter in Hawassa Industrial Park, keeps 100% of its proceeds as a zone firm and is one of Bank A's largest FX sources. Because new foreign banks are spared the 1% asset test for two years, Alpenmeer could open a zone branch early and compete directly for clients like this one.

lessons.title: Strategic impact and partnership options
body: Foreign banks bring global correspondent networks, cheaper foreign currency funding, trade finance know-how and multinational clients who already bank with them abroad. Domestic banks bring branch networks, local deposits, knowledge of Ethiopian clients and regulators, and relationships with exporters and importers built over decades.

The likely early battleground is international business: FDI companies, large exporters, zone firms and diaspora flows. A domestic bank can respond by competing, by partnering, or by a mix: for example accepting confirmation lines and referrals from a foreign bank while protecting ownership of its core exporter relationships. The capstone in Module 5 asks you to recommend that mix for Bank A.

left.title: Threats to a domestic bank
items: Loss of FDI and multinational clients
Competition for exporters' FX
Pressure on trade finance pricing
Poaching of trained staff

right.title: Opportunities
items: Confirmation and credit lines for LCs
Referral and co-lending agreements
Access to a wider correspondent network
Know-how in compliance and systems

scenario.title: An exclusive partnership offer
scenario.situation: Alpenmeer offers Bank A a EUR 40 million LC confirmation line and referral fees for FDI clients, on condition that Bank A refers all its European-bound trade exclusively to Alpenmeer for five years.
scenario.question: What is the strongest response?
options: Accept as offered; the line is valuable
Reject any partnership with a future competitor
Negotiate: accept the line and referrals but on a non-exclusive basis, with client ownership and data protection clauses
Ask the NBE to forbid the offer
scenario.explain: The line and referrals have real value, but exclusivity would tie Bank A's best clients to a future competitor. Non-exclusive terms keep the benefit and protect the franchise.

takeaways: Proclamation No. 1360/2025 and SBB/94/2025 allow foreign subsidiaries, branches, representative offices and share acquisitions
Subsidiaries and branches each need Birr 5 billion; a representative office needs USD 100,000 and cannot do banking business
Eligible parents are listed and widely held or state owned, with three years of reports, a direct home supervisor no-objection and a cooperation agreement
Foreign stakes in a domestic bank are capped at 40% for a strategic investor and 49% in aggregate; 2% or more needs NBE approval
Foreign entry will hit international business first, so domestic banks need a deliberate compete and partner strategy

quiz.q: What capital does a representative office of a foreign bank need?
quiz.explain: SBB/94/2025 requires at least USD 100,000 for a representative office.

quiz.q: In which currencies must a foreign bank branch remit its Birr 5 billion capital?
quiz.explain: The branch capital is remitted in US dollars, euros or pounds sterling.

quiz.q: A foreign subsidiary has a board of 12. What is the minimum number of Ethiopian members?
quiz.explain: At least one-third must be Ethiopian: 12 / 3 = 4.

quiz.q: Within how long must the NBE decide on a complete licence application?
quiz.explain: The process gives the NBE 90 days to decide.

quiz.q: Foreign holders own 20% of a domestic bank. What is the most a new foreign strategic investor can buy?
quiz.explain: The 49% aggregate cap binds first: 49 minus 20 = 29%, below the 40% single cap.

quiz.q: Which test do new foreign banks not have to meet in their first two years when applying for an SEZ branch licence?
options: Capital adequacy two points above minimum
At least 1% of banking sector assets
quiz.explain: SBB/99/2026 waives the 1% asset test for new foreign banks in their first two years.

modules.title: Correspondent relationships and the AML/CFT programme
modules.summary: Run correspondent relationships that foreign banks trust, and an AML/CFT and sanctions programme that meets FATF and correspondent expectations.
objectives: Explain nostro and vostro accounts, SWIFT messages and nostro reconciliation
Complete and review correspondent due diligence using the Wolfsberg questionnaire
Assess de-risking pressure and the bank's AML/CFT programme against FATF expectations
Detect trade-based money laundering, screen for sanctions and report suspicion to the Financial Intelligence Service

lessons.title: Nostro, vostro and SWIFT
body: A nostro account is our account with a foreign bank, held in its currency; a vostro account is a foreign bank's account with us, in Birr. Ethiopian banks settle almost all cross-border payments through nostro accounts at a handful of correspondents in US dollars, euros and a few other currencies.

Payments travel as SWIFT messages: a customer transfer (MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent), and a bank-to-bank cover payment (MT202COV) that must carry the originator and beneficiary details so the correspondent can screen them. Daily reconciliation of each nostro account against the bank's own ledger catches missing credits, duplicate payments and fraud early.

items.label: Order
items.text: Importer instructs Bank A to pay a supplier in Germany

items.label: Screen
items.text: Names, countries and goods screened before release

items.label: Message
items.text: MT103 to the beneficiary bank, cover through the nostro

items.label: Debit
items.text: Correspondent debits Bank A's nostro and pays on

items.label: Reconcile
items.text: Nostro statement matched to the ledger next morning

worked.title: Bank A's USD nostro with its New York correspondent

rows.label: Less: export proceeds credited, not yet in the ledger
Add: duplicate debit by the correspondent, claimed back

worked.note: The unrecorded USD 640,000 credit must be matched to an exporter today, and the duplicate debit claimed from the correspondent.

example.title: An unmatched credit
example.text: Bank A's reconciliation team found USD 210,000 credited to its euro nostro with no matching export permit. The reference named Wollega Pulses Export PLC, but the amount did not match any shipment. Before crediting the client, the team asked for the export documents and found the payer was a third party, which triggered an AML review.

lessons.title: Correspondent due diligence in both directions
body: FATF Recommendation 13 expects a bank that offers correspondent services to understand its respondent's business, reputation, supervision and AML/CFT controls, to get senior management approval, and to be satisfied that the respondent does not deal with shell banks. Foreign correspondents apply this to Ethiopian banks, usually through the Wolfsberg Group's Correspondent Banking Due Diligence Questionnaire (CBDDQ).

Bank A applies the same standard when it opens vostro accounts for foreign banks, including any new foreign bank entering Ethiopia. Answering the CBDDQ honestly and consistently, with board-approved policies behind each answer, is the single best way to keep correspondent lines open.

items.label: Ownership and management
items.text: Who owns and runs the bank, PEPs on the board

items.label: AML/CFT and sanctions policies
items.text: Board-approved, current, tested

items.label: KYC and EDD
items.text: Customer risk rating and enhanced due diligence

items.label: Transaction monitoring
items.text: Scenarios, alerts, STR volumes

items.label: Training and audit
items.text: Staff training and independent testing

items.label: Supervision
items.text: Regulator, inspections, enforcement history

regulation.text: Banks providing cross-border correspondent services should gather enough information about a respondent to understand its business and reputation, assess its AML/CFT controls, obtain senior management approval before establishing the relationship, document each side's responsibilities and refuse relationships with shell banks.

scenario.title: An inconsistent questionnaire
scenario.situation: Preparing Bank A's annual CBDDQ refresh for its euro correspondent, the compliance lead, Yonas Tadesse, finds that last year's answer said all incoming wires are screened in real time, but the operations team confirms screening of incoming wires is still a next-morning batch.
scenario.question: What should he do?
options: Repeat last year's answer to avoid questions
Answer accurately, explain the remediation plan and date, and report the earlier inaccuracy to senior management
Ask operations to stop receiving wires
scenario.explain: Correspondents rely on CBDDQ answers. An accurate answer with a remediation plan protects the relationship; a known false answer risks termination if discovered.

lessons.title: Credit lines, confirmation lines and de-risking
body: Beyond nostro accounts, correspondents provide credit lines that let Ethiopian banks open LCs on deferred terms and confirmation lines under which the foreign bank adds its own undertaking to an Ethiopian LC. Each line has a limit, tenor and price that reflect the correspondent's view of the bank and of Ethiopia.

De-risking is when correspondents cut or shrink relationships because the compliance cost or perceived risk outweighs the profit. Small or high-risk respondents are hit first. A bank manages de-risking by spreading relationships across several correspondents, keeping its due diligence file current, sharing audit and inspection results proactively, and building enough volume to make the relationship worth keeping.

scenario.title: A correspondent gives notice
scenario.situation: Bank A's second US dollar correspondent gives 90 days' notice to close the nostro, citing low volumes and rising compliance cost. It carries 25% of Bank A's dollar payments.
scenario.question: What is the best immediate response?
options: Move all dollar business to the main correspondent and do nothing else
Ask the correspondent to reconsider, while opening talks with at least one replacement and preparing a current due diligence pack
Route dollar payments through a money transfer operator
Stop dollar payments for importers until a new line is found
scenario.explain: Concentration on one correspondent is itself a risk. Engage, but line up a replacement with a ready due diligence pack so clients are not disrupted.

example.title: A confirmation line that reopened a corridor
example.text: Debre Markos Malt PLC needed a confirmed LC to import barley from a French supplier who would not accept Bank A's undertaking alone. A European correspondent added its confirmation under a USD 20 million line after Bank A shared its latest external AML audit. The supplier shipped, and the line has since covered more than 40 LCs.

lessons.title: A risk-based AML/CFT programme
body: Ethiopia's AML/CFT law, reported as Proclamation No. 780/2013, places duties on banks to identify customers, keep records, monitor transactions and report suspicion to the Financial Intelligence Service; a KYC/CDD directive from 2021 sets the detail (its number should be confirmed against the current text). Ethiopia is assessed against the FATF standards through mutual evaluations, and past periods under FATF increased monitoring show how a country's rating shapes correspondents' appetite.

FATF expects a risk-based approach: the bank identifies and assesses its risks, applies stronger measures where risk is higher, and simpler ones where it is lower. In international operations the higher-risk points are high-risk jurisdictions, politically exposed persons, cash-intensive traders, third-party payments, money transfer operators and trade in high-value or dual-use goods.

worked.title: Customer risk rating: Wollega Pulses Export PLC (bank scoring model, illustrative)

rows.label: Customer type: exporter of a commodity with minimum prices
Geography: buyers in one high-risk jurisdiction
Product: retention account, third-party credits seen
Channel: face to face, documents complete
Rating under the bank's model (8 or more is high)

worked.note: High rating means senior approval, source of funds checks on third-party credits and more frequent review.

scenario.title: A politically exposed importer
scenario.situation: Fikru Abebe, a senior regional official, is the main shareholder of a newly formed import company that asks Bank A to open an FX account and a USD 1.5 million LC for construction equipment.
scenario.question: What does a risk-based programme require?
options: Treat it as standard because the company, not the official, is the customer
Apply enhanced due diligence: identify beneficial owners, establish source of funds and wealth, and get senior management approval
scenario.explain: PEPs are not banned, but they carry higher risk. EDD on beneficial ownership, source of funds and senior approval is the expected response.

lessons.title: Trade-based money laundering
body: Trade-based money laundering moves value by misrepresenting the price, quantity or quality of goods. The main typologies are over-invoicing of imports and under-invoicing of exports, multiple invoicing of one shipment, over or under shipment, falsely described goods and phantom shipments where no goods move at all.

In Ethiopia, minimum export prices, ECX trading for coffee and sesame, and Customs records under the Customs Proclamation (reported as No. 859/2014, as amended) give the trade desk benchmarks. An export price well below the minimum or the market, payments from a party other than the buyer, or a shipment route that makes no commercial sense are red flags that must be investigated, not ignored.

worked.title: A sesame export priced below the market

rows.label: Market price at contract date (from market reports)

worked.note: A gap of this size suggests under-invoicing to keep foreign currency abroad, and the trade desk should escalate before handling the documents.

items.label: Mispriced invoices
items.text: Far above or below market or minimum price

items.label: Odd shipments
items.text: Illogical routes, transhipment, vague goods

items.label: Third-party payers
items.text: Proceeds from someone other than the buyer

items.label: Dual-use goods
items.text: Items with military use, licensing needed

scenario.title: Split payments
scenario.situation: Over nine days, a newly opened account of Tana Gebeya Trading PLC receives eleven inward transfers of USD 9,500 to 9,900 each from different senders abroad, described as advance payments for spices. No export permit or contract is on file.
scenario.question: What should the international operations officer do?
options: Credit them; each is below USD 10,000
Return all the money without telling anyone
Hold processing, escalate internally and, if suspicion stands, file an STR with the Financial Intelligence Service without telling the customer
Ask the customer to send one combined payment next time
scenario.explain: The pattern looks like structuring with no trade basis. The officer escalates and the bank reports suspicion to the FIS; telling the customer would be tipping off.

lessons.title: Sanctions screening and suspicious transaction reporting
body: Every cross-border payment and trade document is screened against sanctions lists: the United Nations Security Council lists that bind Ethiopia, and the US, EU and UK lists that correspondents apply to every payment they process. Screening covers parties, banks, vessels, ports and goods, and a potential match is resolved before release, never after.

When staff suspect that funds are proceeds of crime or linked to terrorism financing, the bank files a suspicious transaction report with the Financial Intelligence Service and does not alert the customer. NBE Proclamation No. 1359/2025 also gives the NBE power to freeze funds for up to 10 days (Art. 50). Good reporting is prompt, factual and explains why the activity is unusual.

items.label: Screen
items.text: Parties, banks, vessels, ports and goods

items.label: Alert
items.text: Possible match or red flag raised

items.label: Investigate
items.text: Compliance reviews documents and history

items.label: Decide
items.text: False positive released or transaction held

items.label: Report
items.text: STR to the Financial Intelligence Service, no tipping off

regulation.source: NBE Proclamation No. 1359/2025, Art. 50, and the AML/CFT Proclamation (reported as No. 780/2013)
regulation.text: The NBE may freeze funds for up to 10 days. Banks must report suspicious transactions to the Financial Intelligence Service and keep the report confidential from the customer. Check the current FIS directives for reporting formats and deadlines.

scenario.title: A vessel match
scenario.situation: A coffee export LC for Sidama Highland Coffee Export PLC names a carrier vessel. Bank A's screening system flags the vessel name as a possible match on a sanctions list used by its US correspondent.
scenario.question: What should the trade officer do before negotiating the documents?
options: Proceed, because Ethiopia applies only UN lists
Refer the alert to compliance and resolve it, for example by checking the vessel's IMO number, before handling the documents
Change the vessel name on the documents
Ask the exporter whether the vessel is sanctioned and rely on the answer
scenario.explain: The correspondent will screen the same payment. Compliance must resolve the alert with hard identifiers like the IMO number before the bank acts.

takeaways: Nostro accounts are the bank's lifeline abroad; reconcile them daily and keep payment messages transparent
Correspondents judge the bank through the Wolfsberg CBDDQ and FATF Recommendation 13; accurate answers keep lines open
Manage de-risking by diversifying correspondents, keeping due diligence current and sharing audit results
Apply a risk-based programme with EDD for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions and third-party payments
Screen every party, vessel and good, and report suspicion to the Financial Intelligence Service without tipping off

quiz.q: What is a vostro account from Bank A's point of view?
options: Bank A's account with a foreign bank
A foreign bank's account held with Bank A
quiz.explain: Vostro is 'your account with us'.

quiz.q: Which FATF Recommendation deals with correspondent banking?
quiz.explain: Recommendation 13 covers cross-border correspondent banking.

quiz.q: Which is a classic sign of trade-based money laundering on an export?
options: Proceeds paid by the named buyer
Invoice price far below market with proceeds partly unexplained
quiz.explain: Under-invoicing of exports keeps value abroad.

quiz.q: A customer asks why a payment is on hold after the bank filed an STR. What may staff tell them?
options: Nothing that reveals the report; the bank gives a neutral response
The name of the compliance officer who filed it
quiz.explain: Disclosing an STR is tipping off.

quiz.q: Why must MT202COV cover payments carry originator and beneficiary details?
options: So intermediary banks can screen the underlying parties
quiz.explain: Cover payment transparency lets correspondents screen the real parties.

quiz.q: For how long may the NBE freeze funds under Proclamation No. 1359/2025?
quiz.explain: Art. 50 allows freezing for up to 10 days.

modules.title: Compliance governance and the board briefing
modules.summary: Govern international operations through policy, controls and reporting, then brief the board on Alpenmeer's entry and recommend a response strategy.
objectives: Structure an international operations policy that keeps pace with directive changes
Design internal controls and prepare for NBE inspections and penalties
Build the regulatory reporting calendar for international operations
Prepare a regulatory briefing and response strategy for the board on a foreign bank's entry

lessons.title: The international operations policy
body: A bank's international operations policy translates the FX directives, investment rules and AML/CFT duties into the bank's own rules: who may approve what, which documents are required, which limits apply and how exceptions are handled. Since FXD/04/2026 and FXD/05/2026 moved several approvals from the NBE to banks, the policy now carries more weight than ever.

A good policy is short, owned by a named head, approved by the board, and linked to procedures and checklists that are updated within days of a new directive. It should state the bank's own choices where the directive is silent, such as forward tenors, eligible forward clients and the documents needed for dividend remittance.

items.label: Scope and owners
items.text: Products, units, named policy owner

items.label: Approval authorities
items.text: Who approves dividends, loans, acceptance LCs

items.label: Limits
items.text: Open position, guarantees, forwards, correspondents

items.label: Documents
items.text: Checklists per transaction type

items.label: AML/CFT and sanctions
items.text: Screening, EDD, STR escalation

items.label: Change control
items.text: Update within days of a new directive

example.title: The checklist that was two directives old
example.text: In June 2026, an internal audit of Bank A's trade unit found that two branches still sent acceptance LC requests from retention account holders to the NBE, adding three weeks for clients. Their checklist predated FXD/05/2026. The policy owner introduced a rule that every checklist carries the directive versions it reflects and its review date.

lessons.title: Internal controls for international operations
body: Controls run in three lines. The first line, the international banking and trade units, checks documents and applies maker-checker on every payment. The second line, compliance and risk, sets standards, screens, monitors and tests. The third line, internal audit, gives the board independent assurance.

Key controls include dual authorisation of SWIFT releases, daily nostro reconciliation, real-time sanctions screening, approval files for every bank-approved dividend and external loan, and a daily open position check before close. Each control needs an owner, evidence that it ran and a test that it works.

items.label: First line
items.text: International banking and trade: maker-checker, document checks

items.label: Second line
items.text: Compliance and risk: screening, monitoring, testing, reporting

items.label: Third line
items.text: Internal audit: independent assurance to the board

worked.title: Work assignment: dividend remittance procedure review (sample test)

rows.label: Files sampled from the last six months
Files missing evidence of tax settled
Files omitted from the monthly NBE report
Files with at least one exception

worked.note: At 15% against a 5% tolerance, the control is not working; the review should recommend checklist changes, retraining and a re-test in three months.

scenario.title: One person, two keys
scenario.situation: At a busy branch, the trade officer Abel Girma holds both the maker and checker passwords for SWIFT releases because his supervisor is on leave. He released USD 1.8 million of payments last week alone.
scenario.question: What is the right control response?
options: Revoke the shared access at once, assign a trained checker from another unit, review last week's releases and report the breach
Ask Abel to sign a declaration
Lower his limit to USD 1 million
scenario.explain: Maker-checker exists so no single person can release funds. Restore segregation, check what was released and record the breach.

lessons.title: NBE inspections and penalties
body: NBE inspectors test whether the bank follows the directives in practice, not only on paper. In international operations they typically sample FX sales, export proceeds and repatriation, retention balances, bank-approved remittances and loans, open position reports, and AML/CFT files, and compare them with the bank's reports.

Penalties follow the texts. SBB/96/2025 fines breaches of the open position limit and late or false reporting; FVD/01/2026 provides for fines, confiscation or criminal liability for franco valuta misuse; and the NBE can act on a bank's licence and on individuals it has approved under SBB/89/2024. The cheapest defence is a clean file and an honest, timely report.

scenario.title: An inspector's sample
scenario.situation: An NBE inspection samples 25 export files at Bank A and finds that four exporters received proceeds after the 90-day repatriation period with no follow-up recorded by the bank.
scenario.question: What is the best response from Bank A's management?
options: Argue that repatriation is the exporter's problem, not the bank's
Acknowledge the finding, set up an overdue-proceeds tracker with escalation, follow up the four exporters and report progress to the NBE
Delete the four files from the system
scenario.explain: The bank is expected to monitor repatriation within the 90 days set by FXD/01/2024. A tracker, follow-up and transparent reporting address the root cause.

example.title: A late position report
example.text: One evening, a system outage stopped Bank A from sending its daily open position report on time. The treasurer, Dawit Mengistu, informed the NBE before the deadline, sent the report manually within the hour and documented the incident. Because SBB/96/2025 penalises late and false reporting, the early notice and record mattered.

lessons.title: The regulatory reporting calendar
body: International operations feed many NBE reports. Daily: end-of-day rates and the open position under SBB/96/2025. Monthly: the transactions the bank approved itself under FXD/04/2026, and large exposure reports within 20 days under SBB/87/2024. Interest rate changes on FX-linked products follow NBE/INT/13/2026: rate changes within 5 working days and monthly weighted averages within 7 working days.

A single calendar, with an owner and a backup for each report, prevents missed deadlines. Compliance should reconcile what is reported with what the systems show, because inconsistent reports are often the first thing an inspector notices.

items.label: Every day
items.text: End-of-day rates; open position within plus or minus 18% of Tier 1

items.label: Within 5 working days
items.text: Any change in deposit or lending rates (NBE/INT/13/2026)

items.label: Within 7 working days
items.text: Monthly weighted average rates

items.label: Within 20 days
items.text: Monthly large exposure report (SBB/87/2024)

items.label: Every month
items.text: Bank-approved dividends, profits, external loans and supplier credit (FXD/04/2026)

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. SBB/87/2024, Large exposures
regulation.text: A bank's exposure to a counterparty group may not exceed 25% of total capital, a large exposure means 10% or more, and large exposures are reported monthly within 20 days. Check how the directive treats placements with correspondent banks, such as large nostro balances, when setting correspondent limits.

lessons.tip: Name an owner and a backup for every report on the calendar, and test the backup once a quarter.

lessons.title: Capstone: the regulatory briefing on Alpenmeer
body: The capstone brings the course together. Alpenmeer Bank AG intends to open a subsidiary in Ethiopia and proposes a trade services partnership with Bank A. Your team prepares a regulatory briefing for Bank A's board and a response strategy. The briefing is 40% of the course grade, the test 30%, the work assignment reviewing one international operations procedure against current FX rules 20%, and participation 10%; the pass mark is 70%.

A strong briefing is short and decision-ready: what Alpenmeer must satisfy to enter, how long it will take, which of Bank A's businesses it will touch first, what the partnership offers and costs, the compliance conditions for any partnership, and a clear recommendation with risks.

items.label: Entry rules
items.text: Capital, eligibility, board, fees, 90-day decision, 12-month start

items.label: Timeline
items.text: When Alpenmeer could be live and in which zones

items.label: Exposure
items.text: Which clients and revenues are at risk

items.label: Partnership
items.text: Lines, referrals, terms, compliance conditions

items.label: Recommendation
items.text: Option, conditions, risks, next steps

worked.title: Bank A: international revenue at risk (illustrative, Birr millions a year)

rows.label: FX margin on FDI and zone clients
Trade finance fees from top 30 exporters
LC and guarantee fees from multinational importers
Assumed loss if Bank A only competes: 35%
Partnership referral and line income, net of fees paid
Assumed loss if Bank A partners on non-exclusive terms: 20%

worked.note: Partnering cuts the expected loss from about Birr 319 million to 182 million and adds about Birr 140 million of income, on the team's assumptions, which the board should test.

example.title: How the board read the first draft
example.text: The first draft by Bank A's team ran to 28 pages of directive summaries. The board chair, Tigist Wolde, asked for four pages: the entry rules in one table, the timeline, the revenue at risk, and a recommendation with conditions. The second draft fitted that shape and was approved for discussion.

scenario.title: What goes first in the briefing
scenario.situation: Bank A's board has 20 minutes for the Alpenmeer item. The team has material on entry rules, ownership caps, a SWOT, the revenue at risk and a partnership term sheet.
scenario.question: How should the briefing open?
options: With the full text of SBB/94/2025
With the recommendation and the decision the board is asked to take, then the evidence
With the history of foreign banking in Africa
scenario.explain: Boards decide better when the ask comes first. The rules and analysis then support the recommendation.

lessons.title: Choosing the response strategy
body: Bank A has three broad options. It can compete head on, investing in FX pricing, digital trade services and relationship teams to defend its clients. It can partner, taking Alpenmeer's confirmation lines and referrals on non-exclusive terms. Or it can do both: partner on correspondent and trade services while competing hard for exporters, zone firms and diaspora flows.

Any partnership needs conditions the board can check: no exclusivity, clear client ownership, compliance with the Personal Data Protection Proclamation for any shared client data, alignment of AML/CFT and sanctions standards documented in a correspondent agreement, and exit rights if Alpenmeer's subsidiary starts to target Bank A's core clients.

left.title: Compete only
items: Keeps full control of clients
High investment in pricing and systems
No access to Alpenmeer's lines
Larger expected revenue loss

right.title: Partner and compete
items: Non-exclusive lines and referrals
Client ownership and data clauses
Shared compliance standards
Exit rights if core clients are targeted

scenario.title: The board's decision
scenario.situation: After the briefing, the board must choose. The analysis shows the largest risk is to FDI and zone clients, and Alpenmeer's EUR 40 million confirmation line would cover LCs Bank A's current correspondents decline.
scenario.question: Which recommendation fits the analysis best?
options: Reject any partnership and cut fees to keep all clients
Accept an exclusive partnership to maximise referral income
Partner on non-exclusive terms for confirmation lines and referrals, while investing to defend FDI and zone clients
Wait until Alpenmeer is licensed before deciding anything
scenario.explain: The line fills a real gap, and non-exclusive terms protect the franchise. Waiting would let Alpenmeer reach clients first; exclusivity or pure price cuts destroy value.

lessons.tip: End every board briefing with the exact resolution you want the board to pass.

takeaways: The international operations policy must state the bank's own rules wherever directives leave choices to banks
Three lines of defence and maker-checker controls protect the bank as approvals move from the NBE to banks
Inspectors test practice against reports; clean files and timely, honest reports are the best defence
One reporting calendar with owners and backups covers daily, monthly and event-driven NBE reports
A board briefing leads with the decision, shows the entry rules and revenue at risk, and recommends conditions

quiz.q: What weight does the board briefing carry in the course assessment?
quiz.explain: Board briefing 40%, test 30%, work assignment 20%, participation 10%.

quiz.q: Who gives the board independent assurance on international operations controls?
quiz.explain: Internal audit is the third line.

quiz.q: A sample of 50 files has 4 exceptions. What is the exception rate?
Within how many working days must a bank report a change in its deposit or lending rates to the NBE?
quiz.explain: NBE/INT/13/2026 requires reporting within 5 working days.

quiz.q: Under SBB/87/2024, what is the maximum exposure to one counterparty group?
quiz.explain: The large exposure limit is 25% of total capital.

quiz.q: Which partnership condition best protects Bank A's franchise?
options: Non-exclusivity with client ownership and exit rights
quiz.explain: Non-exclusive terms with ownership and exit rights keep Bank A's core clients.

exam.q: Coffee exporter proceeds of USD 3,000,000 arrive after the MPC No. 7 change takes effect. How much must be converted to Birr?
exam.explain: Goods exporters surrender 30%: 3,000,000 x 30% = USD 900,000.

exam.q: A firm earns USD 200,000 from software services and USD 500,000 from sesame exports in a month. How much may it retain in total?
Spot is Birr 150, Birr rate 16%, USD rate 4%, 180 days. What is the forward rate, to the nearest Birr?
A bank has Tier 1 of Birr 20 billion and a net short USD position worth Birr 3.9 billion at close. What must it do?
options: Nothing; short positions are not limited
Reduce the short position by Birr 0.3 billion by the next business day
Ask the NBE for a waiver within 30 days
exam.explain: The limit is plus or minus 18%: Birr 3.6 billion. The Birr 0.3 billion excess is squared by the next business day.

exam.q: A client wants a 2-year forward. FXD/04/2026 sets no tenor limit. What decides whether Bank A books it?
options: Bank A's own forward policy, credit limits and open position
exam.explain: The directive is silent, so the bank's policy and limits govern.

exam.q: A foreign-owned firm has registered equity of USD 8 million and USD 9 million of external loans. How much more may it borrow abroad under 60:40?
exam.explain: Maximum debt 8 x 1.5 = USD 12 million; 12 minus 9 = USD 3 million.

exam.q: Which document matters most to prove that dividends relate to remittable foreign capital?
options: A letter from the auditor's bank
The Investment Commission registration of the foreign capital
exam.explain: Registered foreign capital is the basis for remittance under the investment law and FX rules.

exam.q: An importer with no FX or retention account asks for a CAD on acceptance. What is the most accurate view?
options: FXD/05/2026's bank approval covers institutions with FX or retention accounts, so the bank must check the rule for clients without one
Any bank may approve it under FXD/05/2026
It must be done as franco valuta
exam.explain: The FXD/05/2026 relaxation is for FX and retention account holders; other cases need the original rules checked.

exam.q: Bank A's total capital is Birr 30 billion and it has Birr 2.8 billion of private FX loan guarantees outstanding. What is the largest new guarantee it can issue?
exam.explain: The cap is 10% of total capital, Birr 3.0 billion; 3.0 minus 2.8 = Birr 0.2 billion.

exam.q: Which foreign investor activity is still closed under Directive No. 1082/2025?
exam.explain: Fertilizer import and wholesale and petroleum import remain closed.

exam.q: A foreign bank's parent is privately held by one family and not state owned. Can it open a subsidiary in Ethiopia?
options: Yes, if it pays Birr 5 billion
Only in a special economic zone
Yes, as long as the board is one-third Ethiopian
No, the parent must be listed and widely held or state owned
exam.explain: SBB/94/2025 requires a listed and widely held or state-owned parent.

exam.q: Foreign investors hold 12% of a domestic bank. What is the most a foreign strategic investor can add?
exam.explain: The 49% aggregate cap binds first: 49 minus 12 = 37%, below the 40% strategic cap.

exam.q: Alpenmeer receives its licence on 1 March. By when must it start operations?
exam.explain: A licensed bank must start within 12 months.

exam.q: What are the two fees an applicant for a banking licence pays under SBB/94/2025?
exam.explain: The directive sets USD 2,500 for investigation and USD 150,000 for the licence.

exam.q: A correspondent asks Bank A whether it deals with shell banks. Which standard is it applying?
exam.explain: Recommendation 13 requires correspondents to refuse relationships with shell banks.

exam.q: Bank A relies on one correspondent for 80% of its USD payments. What is the main risk?
options: Concentration: a de-risking decision would disrupt most dollar business
Lower FX commission to the NBE
exam.explain: Concentration magnifies the impact of de-risking; diversification is the remedy.

exam.q: Wollega Pulses invoices 1,500 tonnes at USD 700 per tonne when the market is USD 1,000. How much value is missing?
exam.explain: 1,500 x (1,000 minus 700) = USD 450,000, a red flag for under-invoicing.

exam.q: A screening alert flags a beneficiary bank on a list used by Bank A's correspondent but not on UN lists. What should Bank A do?
options: Ignore it; only UN lists bind Ethiopia
Ask the customer to change the beneficiary bank's name
Send the payment through another currency
Resolve it with compliance before release, because the correspondent will apply that list to the payment
exam.explain: Correspondents apply their own lists; releasing a payment they will block risks the relationship.

exam.q: An NBE inspector finds three bank-approved external loans missing from the monthly report. Which statement is correct?
options: This is a reporting failure under FXD/04/2026, and the bank should correct the reports and fix the control
No issue, since banks now approve these loans
exam.explain: FXD/04/2026 moved approval to banks but kept monthly reporting to the NBE.

exam.q: Which recommendation best fits a domestic bank facing a well-capitalised foreign subsidiary that offers a useful but exclusive partnership?
options: Accept exclusivity for the referral income
Negotiate non-exclusive terms with client ownership, data protection and exit rights while defending core segments
Wait until the foreign bank has been operating for two years
exam.explain: It captures the partnership's value without handing core clients to a future competitor.

sources: Erudite Africa training module: Ethiopian Context, topic 1.c Ethiopian Regulatory Landscape for International Operations, Level 2 Intermediate (October 2026)

NBE directives as listed in the lessons: FXD/01/2024, FXD/04/2026, FXD/05/2026, FVD/01/2026, SBB/94/2025, SBB/96/2025, SBB/99/2026, SBB/87/2024, SBB/89/2024, SBB/91/2024, NBE/INT/13/2026, and the MPC No. 7 release (13 July 2026)
NBE Proclamation No. 1359/2025 and Banking Business Proclamation No. 1360/2025
Investment Proclamation No. 1180/2020, Council of Ministers Regulation No. 474/2020 and Ethiopian Investment Board Directive No. 1082/2025
FATF Recommendations and the Wolfsberg Group Correspondent Banking Due Diligence Questionnaire (international standards)
AML/CFT Proclamation (reported as No. 780/2013) and Customs Proclamation (reported as No. 859/2014, as amended), to be confirmed against the official texts
